_about: Device-type knowledge for onboard/interview.py: what each shipped check template can emit, which layer each code lives at (decides which questions apply and what 'tell' means), and which shipped remediations a device can be wired to. tests/test_interview.py keeps the code lists in step with the templates' '# Findings:' headers.
_fix_fields: script: the remediation path ({value} = the admin's answer); params: params the fix needs, from the answer; needs: params the admin must set by hand first (a missing one blocks the write); classes: which of fix/ask may wire it (refuse: the reason shown otherwise); questions: which questions accept it (how, host); local_only: it restarts something on THIS box, so a device whose target_host_param resolves to another host refuses it; ends_state: the state the fix leaves the entity in (STATE_MISMATCH with a different EXPECT_STATE is skipped); value_re/value_hint: the answer value's shape; arg: a pinned argument for the ask-first entry; option: the answer form shown in the question; what: the one-line description.

layers.service: the service itself is down - a restart-type fix can apply
layers.state: an entity is in the wrong state - a fail-safe turn_on can apply
layers.host: the host is dark - only a power actuator could act, and only ask-first
layers.chronic: degraded: known-broken, only the admin can clear it; nags at a cadence
layers.credential: a token/cert problem only a human can refresh
layers.upstream: outside the house (WAN) - nothing here can fix it
layers.hardware: software cannot fix a dead outlet or an unplugged disk
layers.sensor: the sensor went blind - page, never act on a blind value
layers.inventory: something changed on the LAN - a human decides if that is fine

_setup_fields: kinds: the short names `interview.py add <name> <kind>` accepts for each check template. Per template, setup: required = params the check refuses to run without; required_any = alternatives, one group must be satisfied; optional = params the check documents (anything else the admin sets is kept with a note - remediation params live in the same block); about = the one-line meaning shown in the setup question; local_question: ask whether the device is on THIS box (keeps being checked while the LAN is down).

about.HTTP_URL: the health URL on the LAN (prefer an IP literal so a DNS outage can't blind the check)
about.HOST_IP: the host's IP, so I can tell 'service down' from 'host down' with a ping
about.HTTP_URL_ALT: a second transport to the same service (e.g. its tailnet URL)
about.ALT_GUARD_CMD: a command that must succeed before I trust the second transport (bin/tailscale-running.sh)
about.HTTP_EXPECT: the status code that means healthy (default 200)
about.HTTP_AUTH_HEADER: an auth header, e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer ...' - reference a token FILE, never paste a token
about.HTTP_TOKEN_FILE: a mode-600 file that exports the header's token

about.TCP_HOST: the host to connect to (IP literal preferred)
about.TCP_PORT: the TCP port that must accept a connection
about.PING_SPLIT: 1 (default) to tell PORT_CLOSED from HOST_DOWN with a ping, 0 to skip the ping

about.OWNER_HOST_IP: the resolver's host IP - when it does not ping, this check stays silent and lets the host's own service report

about.PORT: a local TCP port the unit must answer on
about.LOG_GLOB: the unit's file-log glob, newest file by mtime (for the wedge heuristic)
about.WEDGE_MINUTES: both log sinks quiet this long = wedged (default 75)

about.MOUNT_PATH: the directory that must be a live mount
about.MIN_FREE_PCT: below this much free space I report LOW_SPACE (default 10)
about.MARKER_DIRS: space-separated subpaths that prove the RIGHT volume is mounted
about.REQUIRE_WRITABLE: 1 to report VOLUME_READONLY when the mount is not writable

about.CERT_FILE: a PEM file to inspect - or instead
about.WARN_DAYS: days left at which I start nagging (default 21)
about.CRIT_DAYS: days left at which it becomes a page (default 7)

about.HA_URL: the Home Assistant URL (IP literal preferred)
about.HA_TOKEN_FILE: a mode-600 file that exports HA_TOKEN - never paste the token itself
about.VALUE_LOW: at or below this numeric value I report VALUE_LOW
about.VALUE_CRITICAL: at or below this I report VALUE_CRITICAL
about.EXPECT_STATE: any other state is a STATE_MISMATCH

about.INVENTORY_FILE: the JSON inventory of hosts (self_ip + name/ip/mac per host) I compare the LAN against

systemd.what: restart systemd unit '{value}' on this box

docker.refuse: the docker template takes the container as its single argument, which only an ask-first entry can pin - answer 'ask', or wrap it in a fixed-content script (script:<path>) for the auto class

ha.what: Home Assistant turn_on of '{value}' (fail-safe direction only)

ssh.option: ssh:<user@host> (a forced-command key on that host)
ssh.what: SSH forced-command on {value} (the remote key pins what runs)

outlet.refuse: power-cycling an outlet cuts power - never the auto class; answer 'ask'
outlet.what: power-cycle Home Assistant switch '{value}' (off, wait, on; ask-first; restore trap armed)

script.option: script:<path> [<arg>] (an ask-first entry may pin one argument)

setup.ask: To watch {name} ({kind}) I need: {required}. Give them as KEY=value, space-separated.
setup.accepts: KEY=value [KEY=value ...]  (the keys listed; nothing else yet)
setup.maps_to: params.<KEY> on the new service (CHECK_KEY is set to the service name for you)

extras.ask: Anything else to set on {name}? Its check also understands: {optional}. Remediation params can go here too (e.g. a rate cap). Or 'none'.
extras.accepts: none | KEY=value [KEY=value ...]  (a key the check does not document is kept, with a note)

local.ask: Is {name} on this box itself - so I should keep checking it even while the home network is down?
local.maps_to: local: true on the service (the network gate skips remote services when the gateway is unreachable)

announce.ask: When I run {name}'s fix after your OK, what should the household hear first? Plain words for {who} - what blips and roughly how long; no codes, no 'reply heal'.
announce.accepts: the announcement text, verbatim (one or two sentences)
announce.maps_to: announce on each ask-first entry whose consent is household or named:<person>; the drainer sends it to the announce chat before the fix runs

retire.ask: {name} has been {status} since {since} and nothing has been done about it - is it retired, or still wanted?
retire.maps_to: enabled: false (retire) - the doctrine retirement list either way

class.ask: When {name} breaks ({target}; it can report {codes}), do I fix it silently, ask you first, or just tell you?
class.maps_to: remediations.<code> for its fixable codes ({fixable}); every other code becomes tell-only (null)

how.accepts: systemd:<unit> | docker:<container> (ask-first only) | ha:<switch entity> (turn_on only) | ssh:<user@host> (a forced-command key on that host) | outlet:<switch entity> (power-cycle; ask-first only) | script:<path to your fixed-content script> [<arg>] (an ask-first entry may pin one argument) | none (tell you instead)
how.maps_to: remediations.<code> for {fixable}, plus the params the chosen template needs (REMEDIATION_KEY and the target)

host.ask: If {name}'s host ({host}) goes dark, is there a power actuator I may use - always ask-first - or would acting cut the channel you'd answer me on? The natural answer is outlet:<switch entity> (I cycle its outlet: off, wait, on; ask-first, restore trap armed); or ha:<switch entity> to turn something ON only, ssh:<user@host> for a forced-command key on another host, script:<path>, none, or severs.
host.accepts: outlet:<switch entity> (power-cycle it; ask-first) | ha:<switch entity> (turn it ON) | ssh:<user@host> (a forced-command key on another host) | script:<path> [<arg>] | none (just tell you) | severs (never auto-propose; on-demand only)
host.maps_to: remediations.{hostcodes}: an ask-first entry, null, or a recorded omission (on-demand class) that also goes on the doctrine never-touch list

consent.ask: Whose evening does acting on {name} ruin - just yours, one specific person's, or the whole household's?
consent.accepts: admin | named:<person> | household  (then who/why in your words)
consent.maps_to: consent on each ask-first entry, consent_notes on the service

drill.ask: May I test-cycle {name}'s fix to prove it works - freely, only with your explicit OK each time, or never?
drill.maps_to: the doctrine drill policy (the engine has no drill knob; each remediation's own rate cap backstops it)

nag.ask: When {name} is broken in a way only you (or the ISP) can fix ({chronic} - a router setting, a cable, a renewal, the internet itself), how often do I remind you?
